proof.text: Fix $n\geq1$. The completion projection of [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] identifies $A'/I^nA'$ with $A/I^n$, via the actual structural map. Write $R=\mathcal R_A(J)$ and $R'=\mathcal R_{A'}(JA')$ [def-nagata-rees-algebra]. Apply [lem-per-admissible-modification-system] with $m=n$: for every degree $d\geq0$ it gives $J^d/I^nJ^d\simeq(JA')^d/I^n(JA')^d$. These are induced by $A\to A'$, hence preserve products: the class of $xy$ maps to the product of the images of $x$ and $y$. Taking finite direct sums therefore gives an isomorphism $R/I^nR\simeq R'/I^nR'$ of graded algebras over $A/I^n$. The degree-zero map is the preceding base identification.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, final Note; algebra.tex Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated).

proof.text: The definition [def-nagata-affine-blowup] expresses $Y_J,Y'_J$ as Proj of $R,R'$. By [def-nagata-relative-proj] these are also the affine models of the relative Proj constructions. Apply [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary] to the two quotient base maps: the two infinitesimal fibres are the Proj schemes of $R/I^nR$ and $R'/I^nR'$. No flatness of either quotient or completion map is needed. The graded equivalence of Step 1 induces an isomorphism of these Proj schemes by [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality], proving the first assertion. It is the canonical comparison: on a standard chart at $a\in J$ every degree-zero fraction $x/(at)^r$ maps coefficientwise to its image over $A'$. These are precisely the chart maps of the comparison [def-nagata-strict-transform-blowup-comparison], so the maps agree on the standard chart cover.

source.place: XX 4.4 final Note, printed p.374; constructions.tex Tag 01O3 (lemma-relative-proj-base-change).

proof.text: Write $p_J:Y'_J\to Y_J$ for this comparison. For a domination $b:Y_K\to Y_J$, let $b':Y'_K\to Y'_J$ be its corresponding domination, which exists by [lem-per-admissible-modification-system]. Then $p_Jb'=bp_K$. Indeed both are $X$-morphisms, and on the inverse image $U'$ of $X\setminus V(I)$ both are its structural map to $U$: the blowups restrict to these opens by [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open]. For density in $Y'_K$, [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center] makes $KA'\mathcal O_{Y'_K}$ locally generated by a nonzerodivisor $t$. Its complement is $U'$ because $V(K)=V(I)$; on each chart $R_0\to R_0[1/t]$ is injective, since $t^rx=0$ implies $x=0$. Thus $U'$ is schematically dense. The target $Y_J$ is proper over $X$ by [lemma-nagata-affine-blowup-proper], hence separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Equality follows from [lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated]. Restricting this equality modulo $I^n$ proves that the fibre isomorphisms of Step 2 commute with every domination.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.373, full-support schematic density and domination; p.374, final Note.

proof.text: Put $D_J=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y_J,\bar t_J}$ and $E_J=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y'_J,\bar t'_J}$. The points lie on the closed fibres, so they factor through the closed subschemes $Y_{J,n}$ and $Y'_{J,n}$ cut out by $I^n$. Apply [lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian] to their immersions: their strict-local rings are canonically $D_J/I^nD_J$ and $E_J/I^nE_J$. Step 2 identifies $Y'_{J,n}$ with $Y_{J,n}$ and uses the same separable residue-field closure. Hence its induced map on these strict localizations is an isomorphism. By the structural-map and residue-field uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](3), this is exactly the quotient of $p_J^\#:D_J\to E_J$, not merely an abstract ring equivalence. The same uniqueness applied to Step 3 shows that the maps $D_J\to E_J$ commute with transition maps: the two composites have the same scheme structural map and the same chosen residue embedding.

source.place: XX 2.4.4 proof, printed p.365; algebra.tex Tags 05WS (lemma-quotient-strict-henselization) and 04GU (lemma-strictly-henselian-functorial).

proof.text: The ideals form a set, and their domination preorder is filtered by [lem-per-admissible-modification-system]. Domination maps are unique: two $X$-morphisms $Y_K\to Y_J$ both restrict over $U$ to the identification of [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open], $U$ is schematically dense in $Y_K$ by [lem-per-admissible-modification-system], and $Y_J$ is separated over $X$ (Step 3), so they coincide by [lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated]; over $A'$ use the density of $U'$ proved in Step 3. Hence a composite of dominations is the domination, and the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](3), applied to the compatible points, makes the maps $D_J\to D_K$ and $E_J\to E_K$ compose strictly: both diagrams are functors on the preorder. Thus [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] applies to both ring diagrams. By the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], Step 4 defines the asserted $A$-linear $u:B\to C$. Its quotient modulo $I^n$ is surjective: represent $c\in C$ by $e\in E_J$, and lift its class modulo $I^nE_J$ through $D_J/I^nD_J\simeq E_J/I^nE_J$. For injectivity, represent $b\in B$ by $d\in D_J$ and suppose $u(b)\in I^nC$. Write $u(b)=\sum_{r=1}^h a_rc_r$ with $a_r\in I^n$ and $c_r\in C$. Represent the finitely many $c_r$ at stages and use filteredness to move them and $d$ to one common stage. The equality in $C$ holds at a further stage $L$ by the elementwise equality criterion. There the image of $d$ belongs to $I^nE_L$, so injectivity of $D_L/I^nD_L\to E_L/I^nE_L$ gives $d\in I^nD_L$. Its image in $B$ is therefore in $I^nB$. This proves injectivity and the canonical isomorphism $B/I^nB\simeq C/I^nC$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374, passage to the valuative local rings; the finite-representative colimit argument is written out here. Uniqueness of domination maps: XX 4.4, printed p.373 ('there is at most one').

proof.text: If $IB=(\varphi)$, then $I^nB=(IB)^n=(\varphi^n)$: products of $n$ elements of the extended ideal generate exactly the extension of $I^n$. In $C$, extension along $u$ gives $IC=(u(\varphi))=(\varphi')$, so $I^nC=((\varphi')^n)$. Substituting these equalities into Step 5 proves the last clause. This uses no nonzerodivisor hypothesis on $\varphi$.

title: Congruences of strict local rings on corresponding admissible blowups
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair with $I$ finitely generated and $A'=\widehat A$ its $I$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Set $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $X'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For a finitely generated ideal $J\subseteq A$ with $V(J)=V(I)$ let $Y_J=\operatorname{Bl}_J(X)$ and $Y'_J=\operatorname{Bl}_{JA'}(X')$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup]. The canonical map is the lift of [def-nagata-strict-transform-blowup-comparison]. Then it induces isomorphisms of infinitesimal closed fibres
$$Y'_J\times_{X'}\operatorname{Spec}(A'/I^nA')\xrightarrow{\sim}Y_J\times_X\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^n)\quad(n\geq1).$$
Here the fibre products are those of [def-pc-fibre-product]. Choose a compatible system $\bar t_J$ of geometric points on the closed fibres of the $Y_J$, and the corresponding system $\bar t'_J$ on the $Y'_J$, using the same separable residue-field closures [def-weil-geometric-point]. Define
$$B=\varinjlim_J\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y_J,\bar t_J},\qquad C=\varinjlim_J\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y'_J,\bar t'_J},$$
where colimits have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and use domination of blowups and strict henselizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. The induced homomorphism $u:B\to C$ gives isomorphisms $B/I^nB\xrightarrow{\sim}C/I^nC$ for all $n\geq1$. In particular, if $IB=(\varphi)$ and $\varphi'=u(\varphi)$, these are the maps $B/\varphi^nB\xrightarrow{\sim}C/(\varphi')^nC$.
